1. # **Document Information**

| Project Name | Healing Minds Matter (HMM) Platform |
| :---- | :---- |
| **Document Type** | Initial Requirement Document  |
| **Version** | 1.0  |

| **Scope** | Web Application (Admin & Champion) \+ Mobile Application (Gatekeeper) |

2. # **Executive Summary**

The Healing Minds Matter (HMM) platform is a mental wellbeing initiative designed to improve community mental health through a structured, technology-enabled network of trained individuals known as Gatekeepers. In the long term, the platform will connect people experiencing mental health challenges with qualified professionals. However, in Phase 1, the core objective is to build a strong foundation by growing and managing the Gatekeeper community.

This document defines the complete functional and non-functional requirements for the Phase 1 development of the HMM platform, which includes a Web Application for administrators and champions, and a Mobile Application for Gatekeepers. This document is intended for client review and must be approved before development commences.

3. # **Project Overview**

   1. ## **Background**

Mental health awareness and early intervention are critical to community wellbeing. The HMM initiative establishes a trained workforce of Gatekeepers; individuals certified through QPR (Question, Persuade, Refer) training, who can identify and respond to individuals at risk. The digital platform will support the management, onboarding, and engagement of these Gatekeepers across multiple clubs.

2. ## **Phase 1 Goal**

The primary goal of Phase 1 is:

* Increase the number of QPR-certified Gatekeepers by streamlining the onboarding and management process.

* Track Gatekeeper participation in awareness programs and QPR sessions.

* Provide a centralized platform for resource sharing, event management, and announcements.

* Establish the digital infrastructure that Next Phases (participant and therapist engagement) will build upon.

* Promoting awareness programs and training events.

* Tracking Gatekeeper participation and certification status.

  3. ## **Future Vision (Phase 2\)**

Although out of scope for this document, Phase 2 is planned to include:

* Participant-facing mobile features for individuals with mental health challenges.

* A connected platform linking participants to therapists, psychologists, and psychiatrists.

* Advanced analytics and participant journey tracking.

  4. ## **Application in Scope \- Phase 1**

| Application | Primary Users | Purpose |
| :---- | :---- | :---- |
| Web Application | Super Admin, Champion | Platform administration, resource management, event calendar, dashboards, and Gatekeeper onboarding management. |
| Mobile Application | Gatekeeper | Personal dashboard, QPR session tracking, awareness program calendar, and access to resources. |

 

4. # **User Roles & Responsibilities** 

The HMM platform has three distinct user roles in Phase 1\. Each role has a specific scope of access and responsibility.

1. ## **Super Admin**

The Super Admin is the highest-level user with full access to the platform. This role is typically held by the organization's system or program administrator.

| Attribute | Detail |
| :---- | :---- |
| Access Platform | Web Application only |
| Scope | System-wide (all clubs) |
| Manages | Resources, announcements, clubs, champions, gatekeepers, and system settings |
| Visibility | Can view all champions, all Gatekeepers, all data |

2. ## **Champion**

The Champion is a program coordinator responsible for managing a specific club, onboarding Gatekeepers, and organizing events within their area.

| Attribute | Detail |
| :---- | :---- |
| Access Platform | Web Application only |
| Scope | One Champion is assigned to one club at a time (one Champion, one club). A club can have multiple Champions  |
| Manages | Gatekeepers in their club, events, and announcements |
| Visibility | Limited to their own club's data |

3. ## **Gatekeeper**

Gatekeepers are QPR-certified community members who participate in awareness programs and mental health initiatives. They are onboarded into the system by Champions on their behalf.

| Attribute | Detail |
| :---- | :---- |
| Access Platform | Mobile Application only (Phase 1\) |
| Scope | Assigned to exactly one club at a time |
| Onboarded by | Champion (on behalf of the Gatekeeper after QPR certification) |
| Certification | QPR Certificate; valid for 3 years from date of issue |
| Who can be a Gatekeeper? | Any person; no professional qualification required |

5. # **Web Application Requirements**

 The Web Application is accessible via a standard web browser and is used exclusively by Super Admins and Champions in Phase 1\.

1. ## **Authentication & Access Control**

* All users must log in using a registered email address and password.

* The system shall support Forgot Password functionality via email.

* Authenticated users shall be able to change their password.

* The system must enforce role-based access control (RBAC) so users only access features permitted for their role.

* Session management should include secure logout and automatic session expiry after a defined idle period.

  2. ## **Super Admin \- Features**

     1. ### **Dashboard**

The Super Admin's dashboard provides a high-level overview of the platform's progress across all clubs.

| Dashboard Element | Description |
| :---- | :---- |
| Total Active Gatekeeper Count per Club | Displays the number of Active Gatekeepers currently assigned to each club, giving a quick snapshot of the program's reach. |
| Total Active Champions | Displays the number of Active Champions. |
| Club Onboarding Progress | A visual progress indicator (e.g., percentage or progress bar) showing how far along each club is in getting their Gatekeepers onboarded into the system. |
| Club-wise Gatekeeper Count | A visual progress indicator (e.g., percentage or progress bar) showing how many gatekeepers are onboarded to each club with gatekeeper status (active & inactive). |
| Upcoming Events | Displays the number of Upcoming Events. |
| Total QPR Certified Gatekeepers & Champions | The total count of Gatekeepers & Champions across all clubs whose QPR certification is currently active (not expired), giving a system-wide view of certified capacity.  |

2. ### **Profile Management**

Super Admins should be able to view and manage their own profile information in one place, allowing them to maintain accurate account details and manage their account securely.

* View personal details (name, email address, contact information).

* Update permitted profile information.

* Change password.

* View account role and access level.

  3. ### **Resource Management**

The Super Admin is responsible for uploading and managing all learning and reference materials available on the platform.

* Ability to upload resources of the following types:

  * Videos (upload file or link to an external URL, e.g., YouTube)

  * Articles (rich text content or external links)

  * Documents (PDF, Word, or other file formats)

  * Other file types as may be required

* Each resource should have a title, description, category/tag, and publication date.

* Ability to edit and delete existing resources.

* Resources uploaded by the Super Admin are visible to Champions, and Gatekeepers through the Mobile Application.

  4. ### **Announcement Management**

The Super Admin can create platform-wide announcements to communicate important information to all users.

* Create, edit, delete, and schedule announcements.

* Each announcement should have a title, body text, announcement publication date, and an optional expiry date.

* Announcements created by the Super Admin are visible to all platform users.

  5. ### **Event & Calendar Management**

The super admin can view all the events scheduled in the calendar.

6. ### **Club Management**

The Super Admin is responsible for creating and managing clubs on the platform.

* Create a new club by entering the club name, location, and any other relevant details.

* Edit club details (e.g., update the club name or location).

* Deactivate a club if it is no longer active. When a club is deactivated, all associated Champions and Gatekeepers should be flagged for review.

* View a list of all clubs with their current status (active/inactive) and assigned Champions.

  7. ### **Champion Account Management**

The Super Admin creates and manages Champion accounts and their club assignments.

* Create a Champion account by entering their name, email address, phone number, and assigning them to a club.

* A Champion can only be assigned to one club at a time.

* A club can have multiple Champions assigned to it.

* When a Champion account is created, the system generates login credentials and sends a welcome email to the Champion with instructions to access the Web Application.

* Edit a Champion's details (e.g., name, contact information, club assignment).

* Deactivate a Champion account if they are no longer in the role. Their associated club will not be affected; other Champions of that club remain active.

* View a list of all Champions with their assigned club and account status (active/inactive).

  8. ### **Permission Management**

The Super Admin can manage what each Champion and Gatekeeper roles are permitted to do within the platforms.

* Define and update the set of permissions available to Champions/Gatekeepers (e.g., ability to create announcements, manage events, manage Gatekeepers).

* Enable or disable specific permissions for individual Champions/Gatekeepers or as a default for all Champions/Gatekeepers.

* This allows the platform to be flexible as the program evolves; permissions can be tightened or expanded without requiring a system change.

  3. ## **Champion \- Features**

     1. ### **Dashboard**

The Champion's dashboard is a center-level view of their club's activities and Gatekeeper management.

| Dashboard Element | Description |
| :---- | :---- |
| Active Gatekeeper Count | Displays the number of Active Gatekeepers of their club. |
| Inactive Gatekeeper Count | Displays the number of Inactive Gatekeepers of their club. |
| New Gatekeepers in current month | Display the number of gatekeepers onboarded this month in their club |
| Awareness Program Summary | A summary of awareness programs, including upcoming and completed events. |
| Onboarding Status | A view of Gatekeepers who have been added to the system but not yet logged into the mobile app (if applicable). |
| QPR Certified Gatekeeper & Champion Count  | The number of Gatekeepers & Champions in each club with an active (non-expired) QPR certification, alongside the total count, so the Champion can do a comparison with other clubs to see the QPR certification progress of their club.  |

2. ### **Profile Management**

Champions should be able to view and manage their own profile information in one place, allowing them to maintain accurate account details and manage their account securely.

* View personal details (name, email address, contact information).

* Update permitted profile information.

* Change password.

* View account role and access level.

  3. ### **Gatekeeper Management**

Champions are responsible for adding and managing Gatekeepers within their club.

* Add a new Gatekeeper individually by entering their details (name, email, phone number, assigned club, QPR certification date).

* Bulk upload Gatekeepers from a CSV or Excel file; this is essential for the initial migration of existing Gatekeepers.

* Edit Gatekeeper details (e.g., update contact information or certification date).

* Assign a Gatekeeper to a club (a Gatekeeper can only belong to one club at a time).

* Deactivate a Gatekeeper if they are no longer active.

* View the list of all Gatekeepers assigned to the Champion's club, including their name, contact information, QPR certification date, and certification expiry date.

* View a Gatekeeper's profile, including their QPR status.

  4. ### **Event & Calendar Management**

Champions manage all events associated with their club. Events are visible to all platform users.

* Create new events of the following types:

  * QPR Certification Sessions

  * Awareness Programs

  * Workshops or other community programs

* Each event should include: title, event type, date and time, venue/location, description, and a maximum participant count (optional).

* Edit and cancel existing events.

* A shared calendar view to see all upcoming events across the platform (not limited to their own club).

* Events created by Champions are visible in the Super Admin’s web calendar and Gatekeeper's mobile app calendar.

  5. ### **Announcement Management**

Champions can create announcements targeted to users of the platform.

* Create, edit, and delete announcements.

* Each announcement should have a title, body text, announcement publication date, and an optional expiry date.

  6. ### **Resource Management**

Champions can browse and access all resources published by the Super Admin. 

* Resources can be viewed directly within the app:

  * Articles displayed as readable content within the app.

  * Videos playable within the app or via an external link.

  * Documents viewable through an in-app viewer or downloadable.

* Resources can be filtered or searched by title or category.

6. # **Mobile Application Requirements**

The Mobile Application is designed for Gatekeepers. It is available for both iOS and Android. In Phase 1, the mobile app is exclusively for Gatekeepers. The mobile application will be installed and accessed using credentials provided during the onboarding process.

1. ## **Login & Authentication**

* Gatekeepers log in using credentials (email and password) set up by the Champion during the onboarding process.

* Secure password reset via email or phone.

* Remember login option for ease of access.

  2. ## **Dashboard**

The Gatekeeper's dashboard gives them a personalized overview of their activity.

| Dashboard Element | Description |
| :---- | :---- |
| QPR Session Summary | A summary of QPR certification sessions the Gatekeeper has attended, including the certification date and expiry date. |
| Upcoming Events | A list of upcoming awareness programs. |
| Awareness Programs Joined | A history of past awareness programs the Gatekeeper has participated in. |
| Latest Announcements | A list of latest announcements. |
| Total QPR Certified Count | The number of people with an active (non-expired) QPR certification.  |

3. ## **Events & Calendar**

* A full calendar view showing all upcoming awareness programs and events across all clubs; not limited to the Gatekeeper's specific club.

* Ability to view event details: title, date, time, venue, and description.

* Ability to express interest in or register for an event (if applicable).

* Filter events by type (e.g., QPR Sessions, Awareness Programs).

  4. ## **Resources**

Gatekeepers can browse and access all resources published by the Super Admin. 

* Resources can be viewed directly within the app:

  * Articles displayed as readable content within the app.

  * Videos playable within the app or via an external link.

  * Documents viewable through an in-app viewer or downloadable.

* Resources can be filtered or searched by title or category.

  5. ## **Announcements**

* Gatekeepers can view announcements created by the Super Admin and Champions.

* Announcements should be shown in a clear, easily accessible section of the app.

  6. ## **Gatekeeper Profile Page**

Gatekeepers should be able to see their own profile information; their name, club, and QPR certification details in one place.

* View personal details (name, club, contact information).

* QPR certification date and expiry.

* Edit permitted profile details such as phone number and preferred language.

* Change password from within the profile page.

* Profile changes are saved and reflected immediately upon confirmation.

7. # **Gatekeeper Onboarding Process** 

The Gatekeeper onboarding process is a key workflow in Phase 1\. It is designed to be managed by the Champion on behalf of the Gatekeeper. The steps below describe the end-to-end process.

| Step | Who | Action |
| :---- | :---- | :---- |
| 1 | Gatekeeper | Attends and completes a QPR training session and receives their QPR Certificate. |
| 2 | Champion | Logs into the Web Application and adds the Gatekeeper to the system with their details and QPR certification date. |
| 3 | System | Generates login credentials for the Gatekeeper's Mobile Application account. |
| 4 | System (Optional) | Sends an automated notification (Email or WhatsApp) to the Gatekeeper containing their login credentials and instructions for downloading and accessing the Mobile Application. |
| 5 | Gatekeeper | Downloads the Mobile Application, logs in with provided credentials, and begins using the platform. |

 **Note on Automated Notifications:**

The automated email or WhatsApp notification feature (Step 4\) is optional in Phase 1\. This feature will send the Gatekeeper a welcome message with their credentials and a step-by-step guide to install and log into the mobile app. If time constraints arise, this feature may be deferred to a future phase. 

8. # **Bulk Gatekeeper Data Import** 

Since there are existing Gatekeepers prior to the launch of the platform, a bulk data import feature is required. This allows Champions or the Super Admin to upload a large number of Gatekeepers into the system at once, rather than adding them individually.

1. ## **Requirements**

* Support for CSV and/or Excel file uploads.

* The import template must include fields for: Full Name, Email Address, Phone Number, Club Assignment, QPR Certification Date.

* The system must validate the uploaded file and flag any rows with missing or invalid data before importing.

* A preview of the data should be shown to the user before confirming the import.

* After import, a summary report should show: records successfully imported, records with errors (and the reason), and duplicate records detected.

* A downloadable template file should be available to guide data preparation.

9. # **Language Support** 

The HMM platform will support two languages in Phase 1 to ensure accessibility for a wider audience.

| Language | Application | Scope |
| :---- | :---- | :---- |
| English | Web App \+ Mobile App | Full platform \- all menus, content, and notifications. |
| Sinhala/Tamil | Web App (Only for Champions) \+ Mobile App (Priority) | Mobile App UI and core content. Web App Sinhala/Tamil support to be confirmed based on timeline. |

The system should allow a user to select their preferred language on first login, with the option to change it later from settings. Announcements may be created in one or both languages.

10. # **Recommended Additional Features for Phase 1** 

These have not been explicitly requested but are considered important for the success and long-term value of the platform. Each recommendation includes a rationale.

1. ## **Push Notifications (Mobile App)**

Reason: Gatekeepers need timely reminders to stay engaged with the platform. Without push notifications, key events, certificate expiry alerts, and new announcements may go unnoticed. Push notifications are standard in any mobile application and significantly improve user retention and engagement.

* New event announcements and reminders.

* New resource or announcement notifications.

  2. ##  **Mood Tracker (Mobile App \- If Time Allows)**

Reason: This feature was discussed as a potential addition. A mood tracker for Gatekeepers has dual value: it supports the personal wellbeing of Gatekeepers themselves (who are front-line mental health supporters and can experience secondary stress), and it provides early data patterns useful for Phase 2 when participant wellbeing tracking becomes a priority. If development time allows, this should be included as a basic feature.

* Gatekeepers can log a daily mood (e.g., using an emoji scale or a 1 \- 5 rating).

* A simple history view of their mood over the past week or month.

* This data is private to the Gatekeeper in Phase 1; not visible to Admins or Champions.

*If this feature cannot be included in Phase 1, the data model should be designed to accommodate it in a future phase without significant rework.*

3. ## **Event Registration / Attendance Tracking**

Reason: Currently, the requirement is to show events on a calendar. However, there is no way to know which Gatekeepers attended which events without tracking. Attendance data is valuable for the Champion's dashboard and for the Super Admin's program reporting. Even a simple check-in mechanism (manual by the Champion or self-reported by the Gatekeeper) would significantly increase the platform's analytical value.

* Champion can mark Gatekeepers as attended for a specific event.

* Gatekeeper's event attendance history is visible in their profile and on the dashboard.

  4. ## **Announcement Read Tracking**

Reason: Announcements will be one of the primary communication methods used to share important updates, awareness programs, training opportunities, and organizational information. Without visibility into whether announcements have been viewed, Champions and Super Admins cannot determine if key messages are reaching Gatekeepers. Read tracking provides valuable insight into communication effectiveness and helps identify users who may require follow-up communication.

* The system records whether a Gatekeeper has viewed an announcement.

* Champions can view read/unread statistics for announcements they have created.

* Super Admins can view read/unread statistics for all announcements.

* A summary of announcement engagement may be displayed on dashboards.

* Future enhancements may include reminder notifications for unread announcements.

  5. ## **Audit Log (Administrative Activity Tracking)**

Reason: As the platform grows and more users manage resources, events, announcements, and Gatekeeper records, it becomes increasingly important to maintain a history of administrative actions. Audit logs improve accountability, support troubleshooting, and provide transparency when investigating changes made within the system.

* The system records key administrative activities performed by Super Admins and Champions.

* Logged activities may include creating, editing, or deleting resources, announcements, events, and Gatekeeper records.

* Each audit record includes the user who performed the action, the action taken, and the date and time of the activity.

* Super Admins can view audit logs across the platform.

* Audit logs are intended for monitoring and reporting purposes and are not editable by users.

11. # **Non-Functional Requirements**

| Category | Requirement |
| :---- | :---- |
| Security | All data must be transmitted over HTTPS. User passwords must be stored using secure hashing. Role-based access control must be strictly enforced across all platform areas. |
| Performance | The web application should load key pages within 3 seconds under normal network conditions. The mobile application should be responsive and functional on mid-range smartphones. |
| Scalability | The platform should be designed to accommodate growth — both in the number of users and the volume of resources and events — without requiring architectural changes. |
| Availability | The platform should target 99% uptime during business hours. Scheduled maintenance should be communicated in advance. |
| Usability | The UI for both the web and mobile applications should be clean, intuitive, and require minimal training. Super Admins, Champions and Gatekeepers may not be highly technical users. |
| Data Backup | Automated daily backups of all platform data. Backup retention of at least 30 days. |
| Compliance | The platform should handle personal data responsibly and in accordance with applicable data protection regulations. Gatekeepers should be informed of how their data is used. |
| Device Support \- Web | Compatible with modern versions of Chrome, Firefox, Safari, and Edge. |
| Device Support \- Mobile | iOS 14+ and Android 9+ are the minimum supported versions. |

12. # **Assumptions & Dependencies**

    1. ## **Assumptions**

1. A club can have multiple Champions assigned to it. Each Champion is assigned to only one club at a time. If a Champion needs to move to a different club, their previous club assignment should be updated accordingly. 

2. A Gatekeeper can only be assigned to one club at a time. If a Gatekeeper changes clubs, the system should allow re-assignment and maintain a history of previous club memberships.

3. QPR certification dates are provided by the Champion during onboarding and are assumed to be accurate.

4. The existing Gatekeeper data for the bulk import will be provided by the client in a structured format (Excel or CSV).

5. The automated notification feature (Email/WhatsApp) is treated as optional and will be implemented only if timeline permits.

6. Language selection applies to the UI and system-generated content. User-generated content (resources, announcements) will be in whichever language the author chooses. This will be implemented only if timeline permits.

7. Internet connectivity is assumed for all platform features. Offline mode is not in scope.

   2. ## **Dependencies**

* Email service provider (e.g., SendGrid, Amazon SES) for sending onboarding and notification emails.

* WhatsApp Business API integration (if the WhatsApp notification feature is included in Phase 1).

* Cloud hosting infrastructure for the web application and backend services.

* App store accounts (Apple App Store and Google Play Store) for mobile app distribution.

* QPR certification data from the client for initial bulk import.

13. # **Out of Scope \- Phase 1** 

The following items are explicitly excluded from Phase 1 and are deferred to future phases:

| Item | Reason for Deferral |
| :---- | :---- |
| Participant Mobile App Features | Future Phases will introduce the participant-facing side of the platform. This requires careful design and ethical considerations. |
| Therapist / Psychologist Connect Platform | Future Phase feature. Requires additional stakeholder research, partner agreements, and regulatory consideration. |
| Advanced Analytics & Reporting | Basic reporting is included in dashboards. Advanced analytics (trends, program ROI, health outcomes) are deferred. |
| In-App Messaging / Chat | Not required in Phase 1\. May be introduced in Phase 2 for participant-gatekeeper communication. |
| Payment Gateway | No payment transactions are planned in Phase 1\. |
| Participant Registration | Participants are not users of the platform in Phase 1\. |
